title: Rivers: stream sanity probe
brief: Measure small-stream failures (breaks/sharp/uphill-ridge) with a standalone probe; Commander/opus. Brief attached.

GOAL
A standalone stream-sanity probe for terragen that turns "small rivers look wrong" into numbers, each failure attributed to its cause in channels.cpp.

WHY
Small streams (the Channels levels below the grid's rivers) look wrong in game: they break into disjoint pieces, turn at sharp kinks, and some run along hilltops instead of down toward a river or sea. Before redesigning anything we need counts per mechanism, so the fix job has a check that can fail and we fix the dominant cause first. Agreed target ("sane"): every drawn stream runs unbroken from its head to what it joins, always downhill, never above its banks, never along a ridge. Sinking into fans/sills is not an excuse for now: count it as a break, with its cause.

CONTEXT
- Repo: /home/cody/git/terraverse. Read AGENTS.md first (fixed-point rules, terragen is pure, planet = function of place).
- Stream model: apps/game/src/terragen/channels.{h,cpp}. Header comment explains levels/lattice/nodes. Key code in Channels::read():
  - ~L1160-1190: per-level bend noise (BEND, BEND_SHARE), faded to 0 toward each segment's foot.
  - ~L1268-1288: water is assigned from whichever segment owns the LOWEST land (`owner`), only if seg.flow >= STREAM_FLOW.
  - ~L1378: STREAM_SINKS removes water where land stands above it.
  - later: rolls (ROLLS), beds/benches step(), keep() reshape land after the water is chosen.
  Read gives: land, water, water_gap, water_width, water_from (level), bed, bed_level, relief (-1 floor..1 ridge), slope, pond.
- Node joins are chosen on rough heights (Node::rough_low/high, cost) in build()/toLevelAbove(); sibling/into = tributary of a same-level head.
- Design history: planning/sprint-100-channels.md, sprint-108-water-shapes-land.md, sprint-109-natural-land.md.
- Existing standalone tools to copy the pattern from: scripts/terragen-check/*.cpp (e.g. landscape.cpp, region.cpp, render.cpp), built with scripts/terragen-tool.sh <out> <tool.cpp>. Default world code used by checks: TF22.dGVycmE.

HYPOTHESES TO TEST (Captain's, from reading code; confirm or refute each)
H1 Disjointed: water follows lowest-land ownership, so where a neighbour's hillside (fade ramp, hardness, cirque, rise) comes out lower, the stream's water vanishes mid-run; STREAM_SINKS adds more gaps.
H2 Sharp: segments are straight head->join lines; bend fades to 0 at the foot, so joins and sibling chains kink.
H3 Hilltops: joins picked on rough pre-flow heights, then rolls/benches/rock reshape land around a stream that doesn't know; and/or a fine segment runs along a parent's hillside rather than down it.

APPROACH
- New tool scripts/stream-check/probe.cpp (+ a small runner script scripts/stream-check.sh and a `bun check:streams`-style entry only if package.json pattern makes it trivial).
- For a fixed set of regions (several codes/planet sizes incl. a 100k-radius world and the default; mix of gentle plains and ranges; fixed so runs are comparable), walk the network itself: for each wet node (Channels::node/shape, flow >= STREAM_FLOW), sample along its drawn path (bent as read() bends it) at ~1 block steps, calling read() at each sample.
- Metrics, per level and overall:
  1. continuity: fraction of path samples where read().water is absent or belongs to another level/segment; split the cause: ownership flip (other segment lower), sink (STREAM_SINKS), threshold, other.
  2. sharpness: turn angle distribution along paths and at joins (p50/p95/max, count > 45°/90°).
  3. downhill: water level rising downstream along a path (count, worst).
  4. banks/ridges: water above land within a few blocks either side; path samples with relief > some threshold (on a ridge); fraction of a path where land falls away on both sides.
- Also emit a PNG per region (red = break, yellow = sharp turn, magenta = uphill/ridge over a hillshade) so the Captain and human can eyeball it. Put images in .output/stream-check/.
- Print one summary table; deterministic output.

CONSTRAINTS
- Do NOT modify anything under apps/game/src/ (another agent has uncommitted work in terragen/channels.cpp; don't touch, stash, or revert it). Read-only on engine code. If you need private Channels internals, approximate from public API (node/shape/read/spacing/latticeOf) and say so; if truly impossible, report blocked with what accessor you'd need.
- Match terragen tool style (fixed-point, comments in the repo's voice). No new dependencies.
- Don't commit.

OUT OF SCOPE
Fixing anything. Changing generation, goldens, versions. Planetarium/far rendering (sprint 114).

DONE WHEN
- Tool builds and runs end to end from one command, in reasonable time (state it).
- Summary table of the four metrics per level for each region, with H1/H2/H3 each marked confirmed/refuted/partial with the numbers behind it, and the top cause of breaks named.
- PNGs exist and visibly mark the failures; name 2-3 world coordinates of clear examples of each failure.
- Running it twice gives identical numbers.

REPORT
STATUS / CHANGED / DECISIONS / EVIDENCE / QUESTIONS. Under EVIDENCE include the command, runtime, the summary table, and image paths.

Tool: scripts/stream-check/probe.cpp, scripts/stream-check.sh, package.json check:streams (uncommitted). Findings: H1 confirmed — breaks 46-99%, top cause coarser-level ownership flip (55% of breaks), then same-level (12%), World BANK gate next to grid rivers (23-29% on default), World low-ground gate (77% of 100k plain L1). The network itself is plausible; it just isn't drawn. H2: smooth within segments; kinks at joins (>90° against flow: 25/84, 148/626) and bend folding (fold-area 6-25% L2-6). H3: never uphill; in ranges water perches over a lower bank (61% >0.5 block, p95 34) = same ownership cause. Captain answers to worker Qs: low-ground + BANK gates are in scope (streams must reach their river/sea); owner accessor not needed since the fix stops using ownership for water. Next: phase 2 fix, awaiting human go. Ready to close once human accepts.
